Life is impermanent. Our understanding of the world and our relationship to it is always changing. Things we were taught a few years ago may no longer be true today.

Sometimes, it's hard to let go of what you thought you knew. And sometimes, trying to let go of these things comes with much resistance. It is difficult at times to accept that maybe, just maybe, everything that once stood as the foundation of your life and understanding is no longer true. It is even harder to come to terms with the fact that it may *never* have been true. Some of the things we were taught to be the gospel are in fact just complete fabrications.

Overcoming these stages comes in the basic steps of denial, anger, depression, then acceptance. The issue with reaching the stage of 'acceptance' is trying to reconcile with the actions or behaviors you may have felt during the stage of anger, and the time and vitality lost during the stage of depression. Due to the great amount of dissonance and pain that these transitionary stages can cause someone, many people just prefer to stay in the 'denial' stage, and never go through the burden and the pain of making the transition.

Anyways, perhaps this state of impermanence and mental evolution is what gives birth to an understanding of a 'higher power'. Since the 'truth' never stays the same, our behaviors and understandings are never fully rational or in-tune with reality, so this creates a desire for some sort of means of forgiveness for our past mistakes; in order that you can continue on with life without being constantly burdened by memories of the past. But then again, what may be the case today may not be the case tomorrow.
